rationale: This is a near-rediscovery of the archive's "R&D Cash Runway Commitment" (identical xrd/(dlc+xrd) runway construction and identical first leg up to a 3-month MA), with the only change being +oancf in the numerator — a cosmetic ingredient tweak that also duplicates the (che+oancf) coverage idea already used in "Internal-Knowledge Solvency Mix."

It bolts a genuinely new component (a five-year gross-profit floor, distinct from the archive's oancf floor) onto the archive's best-performing but cross-sectionally weak "R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity," which is a defensible diagnosis-driven refinement, though the triple multiplicative rank risks compressing dispersion and inheriting most of the parent's alpha rather than adding new information.

Mechanically this is the archive's "R&D Adjusted Net-Income Recovery" with DELTA replaced by TS_RANK — a single-operator swap on the same numerator and same first leg, with no economic argument for why a five-year within-firm rank should behave differently other than smoothing.

A level-to-change swap on the archive's "R&D Commitment Equity Cushion," and the change specification is economically ambiguous because rising ceq/lt is driven largely by equity issuance in R&D firms — precisely the channel "R&D External Equity Funding Strain" tested, where the realized alpha sign contradicts the fragility reading and muddies the stated solvency-improvement mechanism.

The cash-burn leg replicates "Goodwill Equity-Cushion Cash Burn," while the added -txt/lt leg is contradicted by archive evidence ("Tax-Validated Goodwill Solvency" produced a negative alpha for positive txt/lt), so the two SUMRANK components likely push in opposite directions and dilute rather than sharpen the signal.

This is "Purchased-Intangible Renewal Deficit" with the second SUMRANK component swapped from retained-earnings deterioration to a (lct-che)/at liquidity gap already used in "Advertising Liquidity Squeeze" and "Goodwill Liquidity Squeeze" — a recombination of two previously tested legs rather than a new mechanism.
